email.body1:
Pat, saw Magic shipped a device verification flow and keeps pushing onchain auth forward with Newton.

When a developer platform expands like that, more accounts come into market than the team can personally cover before they cool off. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Magic off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Pat, quick follow-up for Magic.

In dev-tools, expansion usually means more in-market accounts than reps can touch, and the coverage gap shows up late as a missed quarter. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the number.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Magic needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Pat, last bit of proof for Magic.

Memgraph, another dev-infra company, had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks.

I pulled a benchmark of how Magic's reply rate likely compares to other developer platforms. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Pat, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything, and shipping security and chain features is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a dev-tools motion? I'll tailor it to Magic either way.
